narrative:
The model determined that you have an 82% probability of representing a bad credit risk. This high likelihood led directly to the denial of your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and the level of your savings. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the strongest driver pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. While only 12.6% of approved applicants have accounts in this state, the majority (59.2%) have no checking account at all. This negative status signaled higher risk to the model.

The 48-month duration you requested was the second most important factor and also pushed strongly toward denial. This is more than twice as long as the average 19-month duration among those who were approved.

Your low savings balance (<100 DM) was the third key contributor, further increasing the predicted risk. Nearly half of approved applicants (45.6%) also have savings under 100 DM, but combined with your negative checking account and long loan term, it reinforced the model's concerns.

To improve your chances next time, consider applying for a shorter-term loan, reducing the amount requested, or waiting until you can demonstrate a positive checking account balance and higher savings. Addressing these areas may help shift future predictions in your favor. (218 words)
